# Perspective Audit — Onboarding Wizard

**Component reviewed:** Animated Onboarding Wizard (`OnboardingWizard.jsx`)  
**Escalated perspectives (MEDIUM/HIGH):** Vestibular & Motion Sensitivity, Cognitive & Neurodivergent  
**Perspectives at LOW (not reviewed):** Magnification & Reflow, Environmental Contrast, Auditory Access, Keyboard & Motor Access, Screen Reader & Semantic Structure

---

## Perspective 3 — Vestibular & Motion Sensitivity (HIGH)

### Checklist Review

| Check | Status | Evidence / Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Non-essential animations suppressed under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` | ❌ FINDING | No `@media (prefers-reduced-motion)` anywhere in CSS or JS. Slide transition, icon bounce, and confetti all run unconditionally. |
| Auto-playing content >5s has pause/stop control | N/A | Confetti auto-runs for 3s; no user control to stop early. Not >5s but still unguarded motion. |
| No flashing >3/sec | PASS | Canvas particles are not rapid flashes; they drift downward smoothly. |
| Device-motion gestures have UI alternative | N/A | None present — no shake/tilt triggers. |

### Red Flags Triggered (auto-CRITICAL)

- ❌ `prefers-reduced-motion` media query absent when animations exist → **CRITICAL**

---

#### Finding 1: Unconditional slide transition animation ignores reduced-motion preference

```
**Finding:** Step slider uses CSS `transition: transform 0.5s ease` with no prefers-reduced-motion guard, causing motion for users who have requested reduced motion system-wide.
**WCAG:** 2.3.3 (AAA) — Animation from Interactions  
**Perspective:** Vestibular & Motion Sensitivity  
**Severity:** CRITICAL  
**Route to:** Front-End Dev (secondary: UX Design)  
**Evidence:** `OnboardingWizard.jsx` line 79 — inline style `transition: 'transform 0.5s ease'` applied unconditionally; no `@media (prefers-reduced-motion)` in `.css`.  
**Fix:** Wrap transition in `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .step-slider { transition: none; } }` or conditionally disable via JS based on `window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion)')`.
```

#### Finding 2: Confetti animation plays unconditionally with no reduced-motion suppression

```
**Finding:** Canvas-based confetti animation runs for 3 seconds upon completion with no prefers-reduced-motion guard, triggering motion sickness risk for vestibular users.
**WCAG:** 2.3.3 (AAA) — Animation from Interactions  
**Perspective:** Vestibular & Motion Sensitivity  
**Severity:** CRITICAL  
**Route to:** Front-End Dev (secondary: UX Design)  
**Evidence:** `OnboardingWizard.jsx` lines 19–47 — confetti canvas rendered and animated via requestAnimationFrame when `showConfetti === true`; no media query or JS check for reduced motion. `.confetti-canvas` CSS has no prefers-reduced-motion override.  
**Fix:** Add `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .confetti-canvas { display: none; } }` in CSS, and/or gate the `setShowConfetti(true)` call behind a JS check for reduced motion preference. Consider replacing with static celebratory iconography when motion is disabled.
```

#### Finding 3: Step icon bounce animation runs unconditionally

```
**Finding:** Active step icon uses `animation: iconBounce` on every step change, causing unexpected visual movement even under prefers-reduced-motion settings.
**WCAG:** 2.3.3 (AAA) — Animation from Interactions  
**Perspective:** Vestibular & Motion Sensitivity  
**Severity:** CRITICAL  
**Route to:** Front-End Dev (secondary: Visual Design)  
**Evidence:** `OnboardingWizard.css` lines `.step-icon.active { animation: iconBounce 0.4s ease; }` — no media query guard around the keyframe animation.  
**Fix:** Wrap in `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .step-icon.active { animation: none; } }`. Replace with a static visual indicator like increased border-weight or color change instead of scale animation.
```

---

## Perspective 7 — Cognitive & Neurodivergent (MEDIUM)

### Checklist Review

| Check | Status | Evidence / Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Error messages suggest corrective action | N/A | No form validation present in current component scope. |
| Multi-step forms don't re-ask info | PASS | Step data isn't persisted across steps, but no redundant entry occurs within this wizard itself (each step has unique content). |
| Auth doesn't require cognitive test | N/A | Not an auth flow. |
| Navigation consistent position | PASS | Back/Next buttons always appear in `.onboarding-actions` at bottom-right. |
| Same-function components labeled consistently | PASS | All navigation uses "Back"/"Next" text with aria-labels. |
| Help mechanism same location every page | N/A | No help mechanism present — not applicable to this component alone. |
| Focus doesn't auto-trigger context change | PASS | Clicking buttons triggers explicit state changes; no hover/focus side-effects. |
| Form value change doesn't auto-submit/navigate | PASS | Inputs are uncontrolled (`type="text"` with no onChange); submission only via button click. |
| Destructive actions have undo/confirm | N/A | No destructive actions in this component (Finish just closes wizard). |
| Multiple ways to reach any page | N/A | Single-component scope; not applicable here. |
| Personal data inputs have autocomplete attrs | ❌ FINDING | Name and Role fields lack `autocomplete` attributes, forcing manual re-entry for users relying on autofill/password managers. |
| Timeout warnings ≥20s extension | N/A | No timeouts present. |
| Avoids unexplained jargon/undefined abbreviations | PASS | All text is plain English ("Welcome", "Profile", etc.). |

### Red Flags Triggered (auto-CRITICAL)

- ❌ None triggered — no CAPTCHA, paste blocking, redundant entry loops, or unconfirmed destructive actions found.

---

#### Finding 4: Form fields missing autocomplete attributes for name and role inputs

```
**Finding:** Name and Role input fields lack `autocomplete` attributes, preventing browser autofill assistance and increasing cognitive load for users with memory-related disabilities who must retype common information.
**WCAG:** 1.3.5 — Identify Input Purpose  
**Perspective:** Cognitive & Neurodivergent  
**Severity:** MINOR  
**Route to:** Front-End Dev (secondary: Content Author)  
**Evidence:** `OnboardingWizard.jsx` lines 68–72 — `<input id="name" type="text" />` and `<input id="role" type="text" />` have no autocomplete attribute. Per HTML spec, these should use `autocomplete="name"` and `autocomplete="job-title"` respectively for proper autofill support.  
**Fix:** Add semantic autocomplete values: `<input id="name" type="text" autocomplete="name" />` and `<input id="role" type="text" autocomplete="job-title" />`. This enables browser autofill, reduces typing burden, and aligns with WCAG 1.3.5 AA requirement for programmatically identifying input purpose.
```

## Summary

### Findings by Severity

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| CRITICAL | 3 |
| MAJOR | 0 |
| MINOR | 1 |
| ENHANCEMENT | 0 |

### Perspectives That Passed (All Checklist Items PASS or N/A)

- Cognitive & Neurodivergent — passed all applicable checks except one minor autocomplete gap.

### Findings Grouped by ARRM Role

**Front-End Dev**
- Unconditional slide transition animation ignores reduced-motion preference — Vestibular Motion — CRITICAL — WCAG 2.3.3  
- Confetti animation plays unconditionally with no reduced-motion suppression — Vestibular Motion — CRITICAL — WCAG 2.3.3  
- Step icon bounce animation runs unconditionally — Vestibular Motion — CRITICAL — WCAG 2.3.3  
- Form fields missing autocomplete attributes for name and role inputs — Cognitive Neurodivergent — MINOR — WCAG 1.3.5  

### Open Questions Requiring Human Verification

None identified in this audit pass. All findings are code-level and enforceable from source review.

---

## Recommended Next Step

**BLOCK** — Three CRITICAL findings related to vestibular motion must be resolved before shipping. The component currently provides zero accommodation for users who have enabled `prefers-reduced-motion` at the OS level, exposing them to potentially harmful animations (slide transitions, bouncing icons, and particle confetti). These are not enhancements but fundamental accessibility failures under WCAG 2.3.3 AAA guidance adopted as baseline policy.

Immediate remediation required:
1. Add `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` guards for all three animation sources.
2. Replace motion-based feedback with static alternatives where appropriate.
3. Re-test with reduced-motion enabled in browser dev tools before re-release.
